questions.question: In v = fλ applied to sound, the speed v is fixed by the:
A loudspeaker produces 500 Hz sound in air at 340 m·s⁻¹. The wavelength is:
When a 500 Hz sound passes from air into water, the quantity that stays the same is the:
options: Frequency — the compressions arrive and enter at the same rate, so speed and wavelength change together

questions.question: That 500 Hz sound in water at 1 500 m·s⁻¹ has a wavelength of:

subtopics.title: Sonar — Timing Plus the Wave Equation

questions.question: A sonar echo returns after 1,6 s through seawater at 1 500 m·s⁻¹. The depth is:
The 30 kHz sonar pulse in seawater at 1 500 m·s⁻¹ has a wavelength of:
options: 0,05 m — first convert 30 kHz to 30 000 Hz, then λ = 1 500 ÷ 30 000
0,025 m — the wavelength must also be halved

questions.question: The factor of two in sonar problems applies to:
options: The depth calculation only — the pulse makes a round trip; the wavelength calculation never halves anything
Both the depth and the wavelength calculations

questions.question: Sonar uses high frequencies like 30 kHz rather than 300 Hz because:
options: High frequencies travel faster in water
Low frequencies cannot travel in water
High frequency means short wavelength, and short wavelengths reflect crisply off small objects instead of washing past them

questions.question: Ultrasound is sound with a frequency:
options: Above about 20 000 Hz — beyond human hearing; the syllabus band runs 20 kHz to 100 kHz

questions.question: A bat calls at 68 kHz in air at 340 m·s⁻¹. The wavelength of its call is:
options: 0,005 m — 340 ÷ 68 000, about the size of a moth

questions.question: A moth is 1,7 m from a bat. The bat hears its echo after:
options: 0,01 s — the round trip is 3,4 m, and 3,4 ÷ 340 = 0,01

questions.question: A dolphin clicking at 75 kHz in seawater at 1 500 m·s⁻¹ produces wavelengths of:
options: 0,02 m — 1 500 ÷ 75 000, fine enough to pick out a single fish

subtopics.title: The Ear's Limits, and Ultrasound in Medicine

questions.question: The human ear is most sensitive:
options: In the middle of its range, around speech frequencies — sounds near the extremes need larger amplitude to seem equally loud
At the very top of its range, near 20 kHz

questions.question: An ultrasound scanner builds its image by:
options: Passing sound straight through the body onto a film
Timing the echoes reflected at boundaries between different tissues and converting each time to a depth
Detecting sounds the organs make themselves

questions.question: An echo from a tissue boundary 0,06 m deep, with sound at 1 500 m·s⁻¹ in the body, returns after:
Ultrasound is chosen over X-rays for prenatal scans because ultrasound:
options: Gives sharper pictures in every situation
Is a mechanical pressure wave, not ionising radiation, so it does not damage cells

questions.question: Thunder arrives 3 s after the lightning flash. The storm is about:
options: 1 020 m away — 340 × 3, with NO halving, because the sound made a one-way trip

questions.question: The question that decides whether to halve a sound calculation is:
options: Did the sound return to where it started? Round trip — halve; one-way — do not

questions.question: Louder thunder crosses town:
options: At the same 340 m·s⁻¹ — speed belongs to the air, not the source

questions.question: A wave reflects usefully off an object when the object is:
options: About the size of the wavelength or bigger — long waves flow around small objects like swells around a jetty pole

questions.question: Bats squeak at very high frequencies because:
options: High pitch scares the moths into flight
Higher frequency means shorter wavelength, and only moth-sized waves bounce off moths
High frequencies are louder in air
Low frequencies would use too much energy

questions.question: A bat hears its squeak return after 0,01 s. With sound at 340 m·s⁻¹, the moth is:
options: 1,7 m ahead — the 3,4 m round trip, halved

questions.question: An ultrasound scanner is like a torch because it:
options: Bounces waves off things and builds a picture from what comes back — but its waves are sound, not light
Warms the body as it scans

questions.question: Echoes form inside the body wherever the pulse:
options: Crosses a boundary between different tissues — part of the pulse reflects back at each one

questions.question: Besides imaging, focused ultrasound is used to:
options: Break kidney stones into fragments the body can pass — pressure waves doing surgery with no cut
